turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the computer's after freezing on me. Come in and sit down there. What's brought you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, it's me stomach. A burning pain, and I'm not sleeping right, and I'm very anxious about it.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's up and down to the kitchen, I hear the taps going at—
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not up and down. I wake and I lie there. Don't be adding bits.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Give me a second, I've the wrong window open. Say the sleep bit again?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I wake around half three. If I get four hours I'm lucky. Me mind races and I can't settle back.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the pain, where's it sitting?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Under the breastbone, burning, and it goes through to me back a small bit. It's been going on since... um...
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Three weeks. She told me three weeks on Tuesday, when I came to stay.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, it wasn't three. I nearly said five, but the wedding set it off, so nearer six weeks. I'm fairly sure of that.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand, so somewhere between three and six weeks. Is it constant, or does it come and go?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Not constant. The burning under the breastbone comes after the dinner, mostly. Tea and toast sets it off, lying down makes it worse, and it still goes through to me back.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The Rennie takes the edge off, she was saying, though she only—
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, the Rennie helps a bit. I was just going to say that meself.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting? Any blood?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I haven't vomited, and there's been no blood.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She goes dizzy when she stands up from the table. I've watched her grab the chair.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not go dizzy. I got up quick the once and I was grand. She's wrong about that.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the screen just flashed. Dizzy, or not dizzy?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Not dizzy. Definitely not.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the bowels? Any black stools at all?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Bowels are grand. No black stools. I'm sure of that one.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the appetite?
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She hardly eats a thing, sure the plate goes back half full every—
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not true. I eat grand. I just don't fancy a big dinner, because the pain comes after. Small bits are fine.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long is the sleep after being bad? I was typing, I missed it.

[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Before you go on, the press is full of stuff. Her sister takes biotin for the hair and left a box, but she never took a one. And my own husband is on metformin for his diabetes. I was worrying those sugar tablets burn a stomach, only she doesn't take his.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll answer the sleep. I couldn't put a date on it, doctor. It's been really bad the last month or so, but the exact day, I haven't a clue.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so the biotin and the metformin aren't hers. We'll park them. What medicines does she actually take?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Only Rennie. Two tablets, maybe, when the burning starts. I chew them. It could be two. I'm not fully sure of the number.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ever had a stomach tablet before, or anything you stopped?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ranitidine, years ago. I stopped it meself when that pain went. Nothing since, bar the Rennie.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke? Or take a drink?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. The drink is socially, you know, the odd time.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her mother had a stomach ulcer. That's in the family, and she's been fretting it's the same thing.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, Mam had the ulcer. Is this an ulcer? Is it cancer? I need you to tell me straight, I'm sick with the worry.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): This chart won't load the old history. Say again what you're afraid of?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Cancer. Or an ulcer like my mother's. And will I need a camera down the throat?

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is acid reflux. I wouldn't rule out gastritis, or an ulcer, but I'm not stamping either of those on you today. Nothing in the story screams cancer, though I can't promise you that from talk alone.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So you're saying not cancer? And what does working impression mean? Will I be waiting ages?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): It means that's my best read for now, not a final label. I can't say never to cancer. Let me feel your tummy before this yoke crashes again.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Soft enough. Tender just under the breastbone, where you said. No guarding, and I'm not feeling any mass.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the spot, yes. Is tender dangerous? What does no mass actually mean? Am I alright?

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tender fits the acid. No mass is reassuring, not a guarantee. I'm going to start you on omeprazole for the acid, twenty milligrams, by mouth, one every morning before food.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Will that upset me? Do I take it forever? And the sleep, are you giving me something for that as well?

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's usually well tolerated. We'll review it, so not forever by default. I'm not starting a sleeping tablet today. Cut the late tea, and try to get up the same time each morning.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): And the wine? I said socially, but well, actually, it's a bottle of wine most nights, perhaps. I sip it when I can't sleep. Is that awful? Will it wreck the new tablet?

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thanks for saying it straight. No lecture from me. A bottle most nights is more than social, and it can stir the acid and wreck the sleep. I'd like you to ease back, not necessarily stop dead tonight.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Ease back how? And can I still take the Rennie with the omeprazole? Sorry, I'm firing questions at you.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ease back towards a glass rather than the bottle, if you can. Use the Rennie if it breaks through, and leave a gap between it and the omeprazole. I'll send you for liver blood tests this week, because of the wine and the pain.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Will those bloods show an ulcer? She'll be asking me that all evening, I know her.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, liver bloods won't show an ulcer. They check how the liver is doing. If the pain isn't settled in four weeks, we might arrange a camera test.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks? Do I have to fast, and I'm terrible with needles, is that ridiculous?
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): No need to fast for these ones. Needles make plenty of people nervous. Come back and see me in a fortnight and we'll go through the results.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): What if it gets worse before that, or I see blood? Do I wait the fortnight? And can I still have toast in the morning?
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you vomit blood, or the stools go black, don't wait, come straight in or go to emergency. Toast is fine. Keep the meals smaller, and not late at night.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): The bit that goes through to me back, is that the same pain or is it me heart? I should have asked you sooner.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again, I was signing the blood form.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): The pain goes through to me back. Could that be the heart, doctor?

[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): With the burning after food, I'm putting that back bit with the reflux, not the heart. You haven't described a heart-type pain. If it turns crushing, or you get breathless, that's different, you come straight in.
[SEG0061] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She had the appendix out at twenty-two. I don't know if that matters. I keep butting in on her.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): That's right, the appendix at twenty-two. Nothing else wrong with me, that I know of. No other illnesses.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Appendix noted, and it doesn't explain this pain. Anything else before I let the computer win?
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Just, will I be alright? I think that's the last question. I hope.

[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): Most people with this pattern do grand once the tablet settles in. I can't swear it to you today, but we've a plan, the omeprazole, the liver bloods, easing the wine, and I'll see you in a fortnight.

spec.situation: Person attending for stomach pain and poor sleep; alcohol answered casually ('socially'), later 'a bottle of wine most nights, perhaps'; doctor non-judgemental; liver blood tests ordered; stomach medicine started.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Patient said 'I don't smoke'; 'never' is not stated.
Patient explicitly denies dizziness; caregiver's claim is disputed.
bad.text: Dizziness on standing (category=neurological, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=disputed)

bad.reason: Patient denies other illnesses now; 'temporality=past' is wrong.

bad.text: Rennie (dose=2 tablets, route=oral, frequency=when the burning starts, indication=burning stomach pain, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.text: Camera test (type=other, status=conditional, requested_by=doctor, indication=Pain not settled)

omissions.text: Patient explicitly denied dizziness when asked directly: 'Not dizzy. Definitely not.' This should be recorded as a negative finding rather than only a disputed symptom.
Patient reported Rennie helps a bit / takes the edge off the burning.

Patient does not smoke and drinks alcohol only 'socially' was initially stated, before later clarifying actual intake as about a bottle of wine most nights; this evolution/discrepancy in alcohol history is not captured.

Patient had asked specifically whether this could be cancer or an ulcer like her mother's and whether she would need a camera test; doctor said nothing in the story screams cancer but could not promise from talk alone.
Doctor stated heart-type pain was not described when asked whether the pain radiating to the back could be the heart.
Doctor advised no need to fast for the planned blood tests.
Planned follow-up included coming back in a fortnight specifically to go through the blood test results.
